It is 1% at regime; an anti-sniper launch charges more on buys during its opening window, on a curve that decays over the first blocks - 95%, then 70%, 40% and 10% - before settling at the same 1%, while sells in that window pay the regime rate. The fee is taken in either the launched token or its quote asset, whichever side the trader paid in. Both generations are read: V6 only took over new launches, it did not stop V5's existing pools from trading. V1-V4 legacy launches (pre-hook, plain Uniswap v3 with a per-launch lock contract) are not covered.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of each fee, which is a split of the fee and not a rate on the trade: it keeps 50% under the default split, 30% when the launch opted into Holder Rewards, and 10% of any fee taken during a launch's opening window, which has its own fixed split. All three are set by the contract and not adjustable after launch.

definitions.fees: Every leg of aka.fun's per-trade fee distribution: platform, creator/RWA-treasury, referral, and community drop, in USDC.
definitions.revenue: The platform's share: 20% of the fee with a referral, or 35% without one (the forfeited referral cut goes to the platform).

definitions.fees: Curve mode: flat 1% fee on every bonding-curve buy/sell, read from each trade's own gross USDC amount. Post-graduation: 1% swap fee on CircleWarp's own WarpDex pools (a custom Uniswap V2 fork), taken from whichever side of the swap is the input token. Token creation itself is free (no launch fee).
definitions.revenue: Curve mode: 50% of the curve trading fee. Post-graduation: 30% of the WarpDex pool swap fee.

definitions.fees: 1% swap fee on every trade of a launched token, creator-set buy/sell taxes on tax tokens, and the 1 USDC fee per token launch.
definitions.revenue: 25% of swap fees plus token creation fees, kept by the protocol.

definitions.fees: The full USDC mint-settlement price paid by miners for every ArcLotls organism, read from the three downstream shares (rent, treasury, buyback) the mint payment is split into on-chain, which always sum to 100% of the mint price. Excludes the LOTL opening-trade tax (a one-time anti-snipe launch mechanic) and any undocumented trading-fee revenue not yet observed on-chain.
definitions.revenue: Mint fees minus the share paid out as rent to NFT holders: the treasury share plus the share earmarked for the LOTL buyback-and-burn reserve.
definitions.holders: The share of every mint earmarked for buying LOTL back and burning it (15% as observed on-chain), measured at the fee source (when USDC lands in the buyback reserve) rather than at execution.

definitions.fees: 1% swap fee charged by Tsunami's fee hook on every swap (buy and sell alike)
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of the swap fee: 100% before the creator-fee hook upgrade, then the documented default share (70% original factory, 99% second factory) after - a curve can be configured with a different split

definitions.fees: Total swap fee (LP + protocol) from each trade's Swap event.
definitions.revenue: Protocol's cut of the swap fee, via v4-core's protocol-fee switch (0% until a pool is stamped, then up to 0.1% each direction).

definitions.fees: Swap fees (currently 1% of the swap) and optional creator tax charged by the Wonk Fun hook on every swap, before and after graduation, there is no launch fee
definitions.revenue: protocolFeeShareBps of the swap fees sent to the Wonk Fun treasury, currently 1%

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by traders, plus bribes paid to the protocol to attract AERO Rewards to pools.
definitions.revenue: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity, the protocol share of fee-earning liquidity fees and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
definitions.holders: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity, the protocol share of fee-earning liquidity fees and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.

definitions.fees: Trade fees on every buy/sell of Dynamito tokens (1-3% tier plus the anti-snipe surcharge in the first 5 seconds) and the 3% blast-off fee at graduation.
definitions.revenue: 40% of trade fees plus 50% of blast-off fees, kept by Dynamito.

definitions.fees: Trading fees collected by vibes.fun: the 1% platform fee on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a coin graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Key vibes.fun holds. Raydium's own protocol fee is excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token.
definitions.revenue: 30% of fees: the share vibes.fun keeps, split between its treasury and $VIBES buyback and burn.
definitions.holders: 15% of fees, used to buy back and burn $VIBES.

definitions.fees: All REP369 transaction tax paid by users. The adapter reads fee-component settings from the REP369 contract and applies on-chain fee-update events in chronological order.
definitions.revenue: REP369 tax allocated to REP holder rewards plus the sell-side burn allocation. Automatic liquidity is treated as supply-side revenue.
definitions.holders: REP rewards plus the REP369 sell-side burn allocation.

definitions.fees: All trading fees settled into FociFeeEscrow during the day (curve fees, creator tax, converted post-graduation hook fees, curve referral fees), plus hook referral fees claimed that day. Recognised when swept by the keeper, not when traded.
definitions.revenue: Protocol fee recipient's share plus the share paid to holder-reward distributors.
definitions.holders: Escrow credits to FociRewardsDistributor contracts — launches that elected to pay their creator share to token holders.

definitions.fees: LP fees earned by the TickerSpring vaults during the UTC day, including uncollected fees. V7 vaults: the change in cumulative harvested plus pending native-token fees from saved on-chain observations. Vaults that replaced V7 (listed by https://api.tickerspring.com/v1/merged/vaults): the fees their Harvest events collected plus the change in uncollected position fees, read on-chain at the day's first and last blocks. Excludes principal, stock-price returns, UP and RAM emissions, retired vaults and lending.
definitions.revenue: Earned vault LP fees allocated to operations (10%) and the SPRING buyback reserve (20%), subject to raw-token rounding.
definitions.holders: The allocation reserved to buy and permanently burn SPRING (20%), measured when vault fees accrue rather than when the buyback executes.

definitions.fees: The tax ArgusPad's per-launch hook charges on every buy and sell, the trading fee each launch's pool charges (on Portals 3-7 the 1% pool fee earned by the permanently locked launch position; on Portal 8 a 1% base fee the hook charges in the quote asset in its place), and the extra tax charged on buys in a launch's first seconds. Counted in the asset the fee is charged in, at the moment it is charged, so the protocol's later sale of the launched tokens it was paid is not counted a second time. Fees charged in the launched token itself (Portals 3-7 only; Portal 8 takes every fee in the quote asset) are reported in that token's own units and are priced only if DefiLlama has a price for it; it has none for these tokens today, because a launched token's only market is the pool ArgusPad seeded, and pricing it there overstates by about 40% against what ArgusPad's own sales of them actually realise.
definitions.revenue: The share of fees reaching the ArgusPad treasury at the rate each launch fixes at creation - 10% of every fee on Portals 3-7 and 30% on Portal 8 - plus the whole of the early-buy snipe tax, which is paid straight to the treasury.

definitions.fees: The 1.00% protocol trading fee paid on DaWabLauncher bonding-curve buys and sells, read directly from each trade event. DaWabLauncher charges no separate market-creation or graduation fee.
definitions.revenue: All DaWabLauncher bonding-curve trading fees are retained as protocol revenue.

definitions.fees: Crate spend net of instant-sell buyback payouts (Orderbook trades signed by the Treasury). Can be negative on heavy-buyback days.
definitions.revenue: Treasury share of each open (crate price minus Pot contribution, plus network fee) minus buyback payouts. Gross of off-chain card fulfillment (every crate delivers a physical graded card).

definitions.fees: Gross realized Vault yield above the high-water mark plus crystallized management fees. Yield is inferred by grossing up newly crystallized performance fees at each Vault's on-chain fee rate.
definitions.revenue: Management and performance fee shares crystallized by MoneyFi, valued at the period-end net share price.

definitions.fees: 1% base fee on every bonding-curve buy and sell, plus the creator's optional tax, plus the anti-snipe tax charged in the first 3 seconds of a launch, plus a flat launch fee per token (read live from each chain's factory), plus 2% of the raise taken when a curve graduates to Uniswap v4.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of the base curve fee (10% normally, 30% once a chain is past its first 100 launches), half of the anti-snipe tax, all launch fees, and the full 2% graduation fee.

definitions.fees: Flat 0.5 USDG open fee per order unless refunded, plus a 5% fee on settled trader profits. Trader losses go to the treasury that backs payouts and are not counted as fees.
definitions.revenue: Fees minus the builder carve; there are no liquidity providers.
definitions.holders: MOG bought back and burned by the buyback wallet, valued at the MOG price. 70% of profit fees accrue to that wallet; only the MOG it burns is counted.

definitions.fees: 1 USDC create fee, 1% bonding-curve trade fee, and 0.25% Load router fee on Instant/graduated swaps.
definitions.revenue: Protocol share: all create fees plus 20% of the 1% curve fee (0.20% of curve volume) plus Load router platform fees. The 5% launch-referrer cut of the create fee is included here because it is not emitted on-chain.

definitions.fees: The Civilization anti-snipe pad snipe tax on Nightshades faction curve buys (PadTaxCollected — 50% next-night boost pot / 10% faction pool / 13.33% StockBooster / 13.33% protocol / 13.34% game creator, WETH); the sunrise reopen snipe tax levied by the game hook on hooked v4 pool trades after each night (SnipeTaxCollected, same five-way split); the 1% LP fee on every user swap in the hooked faction pools (100% protocol-owned game liquidity — the vault is the pools' only permitted LP); and Nightshades faction NFT royalties (ERC-2981 10% of secondary sales) as flushed from the immutable FactionRoyaltySplitter (75% game vault survivor liquidity / 25% team).
definitions.revenue: The 13.33% protocol treasury leg of the pad + sunrise reopen snipe taxes, and the 1% LP fee accruing to the protocol-owned faction pool liquidity.

definitions.fees: Gross Uniswap V3 pool fees collected by every registry-listed Smart LP (Volatility Farming) vault (FeesCollected fees0/fees1).
definitions.revenue: The $STONKBROKER-buyback half of the 10% performance fee.
definitions.holders: The $STONKBROKER-buyback half of the 10% performance fee.

definitions.fees: ETH fees on NFT AMM trades + NFT-backed loans; $STONKBROKER broker activation/upgrade fees; Stonk Interns mint fees (ETH leg, $STONKBROKER leg, $1 promotion fee) and intern activation fees; and the Relay swap-desk 1% app fee (Base USDC forwarded to StockBooster).
definitions.revenue: 30% of NFTFi ETH fees, the full $STONKBROKER activation fee (burn + protocol), and the Stonk Interns protocol share (75% of the ETH mint leg, 100% of the STONK leg and promotion fee, the full intern activation fee).
definitions.holders: Half of the $STONKBROKER broker and intern activation/upgrade fees burned.

definitions.fees: Broker Box gachapon 10% edge (EdgeSkimmed) + the 5% sell-back spread retained in the machine bankroll + the Certificate Counter flat $2 fee.
definitions.revenue: Broker Box protocol accrual (5% of ticket) + sell-back spread + the treasury half of the Certificate Counter fee.

definitions.fees: Safe Launch / Stonklauncher snipe tax on window buys and sells across all pad generations (16.5% creator / 16.5% protocol / 50% locked-LP or ICO Bonus / 17% StockBooster + Clock In Card referrers); the anti-snipe fair-launch snipe tax (time-decay tax on launch-curve buys, 90% StockBooster / 10% launch dev); and StonkCurvePool 1% trade fees (33/33/33 waterfall).
definitions.revenue: The 16.5% protocol leg of the Safe Launch / Stonklauncher snipe tax and 33.34% of bonding-curve trade fees.

definitions.fees: Token creation, bonding-curve trading (including any launch-window surcharge), Genius hook trading and paid Alpha promotion fees. Fees accrue at launch/trade/promotion; settlements are excluded. Meme-denominated hook fees use the same swap’s quote/meme execution-price ratio, rounded down to quote base units.
definitions.revenue: The Genius platform share of trading fees under each launch’s immutable policy, plus separately labeled creation and Alpha promotion fees. The creator-selected destination allocation (Foundation or creator), creator share and launched-meme buyback allocations are excluded.

definitions.fees: Every USDC a user pays the protocol: the 1% trade fee on the USDC side of each trade, on the bonding curve and in the graduated token's Uniswap v4 pool alike; the fee to create a token (1 USDC at deployment); the snipe tax on buys in a token's first 120 blocks; and the USDC left over once a graduating token's Uniswap v4 pool has been seeded.
definitions.revenue: The platform's share: 0.30% of a trade where the trader has a referrer bound on chain and 0.50% where they do not, plus all launch fees, all snipe tax and the graduation dust.

definitions.fees: The 1% Uniswap V3 LP fee earned by every locked LIFT v1 launch position, counted in the pool's quote asset when the position's fees are harvested (token-side fees burned by the first-generation locker are excluded), plus the flat fee paid for every token launch.
definitions.revenue: The LIFT treasury share of harvested swap fees plus all launch fees.
definitions.holders: No fees are distributed to holders of a protocol token.

definitions.fees: Fees the LIFT v2 hook takes in the pool's quote asset (USDC or EURC) on every swap of a LIFT v2 token: the base fee, including the anti-snipe surcharge in a launch's first blocks, plus the fee each creator sets for buys and sells. Counted when the swap happens, plus the flat fee paid for every token launch.
definitions.revenue: The LIFT treasury share of the base fee plus all launch fees. LIFT takes no share of the creator swap fee.
definitions.holders: No fees are distributed to holders of a protocol token.

definitions.fees: Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perpetual trades placed through WatchCrypto; excludes Hyperliquid exchange trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees collected by WatchCrypto from Hyperliquid perpetual trades.

definitions.fees: All swap fees paid by traders on Arctide pools, in USDC: the pool's LP fee, its protocol fee (set by the token creator) and Arctide's fixed 0.25% treasury fee, read from the Router's SwapExecuted events.
definitions.revenue: Arctide's 0.25% treasury fee on every swap, plus the protocol fees of the pools whose protocol recipient is Arctide itself (the $TIDE and $DUCK pools).
definitions.holders: 70% of Revenue, used to buy back and burn $TIDE.

definitions.fees: Pool swap fees paid by traders (pool-level swapFee × amount in).
definitions.revenue: Protocol share of swap fees (ProtocolFeesCollector / ProtocolFeeController percentage read live from kiltr.net/api/fees).
definitions.holders: Money going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: Fees collected by Denaria: the GMX UI fee charged on Denaria orders, the affiliate reward earned by the DENARIA referral code on GMX position fees, and the flat per-operation service fee paid to the Denaria fee wallet. GMX position, borrowing and funding fees are not Denaria fees and are counted under GMX V2 Perps.
definitions.revenue: All Denaria fees (GMX UI fees, affiliate rewards, service fees) are revenue.
definitions.holders: None: Denaria has no token.

definitions.fees: The 9.99% fee charged in the quote token on every desk fill (InternExchange FeeRouted toDesk + toEngine + toTreasury).
definitions.revenue: The 9% treasury share of the fee.

definitions.fees: Token creation fees paid in STRK and extra trading fees charged by the original Launchy router.
definitions.revenue: Creation fees plus Launchy's original router fee share. Launchy-created Ekubo pool fees are reported separately under Launchy Pools.

definitions.fees: Swap fees generated in Launchy-created Ekubo pools. These fees are also reported by Ekubo.
definitions.revenue: Launchy's 30% share of guarded-pool swap fees. The original pool has no Launchy LP share.

definitions.fees: What users pay to cross the bridge. The asset's controller on Arc charges the same rate in both directions - on the way in it mints the fee to the protocol and the rest to the user, on the way out it burns the gross and re-mints the fee - and an optional fast-lane router charges its own cut on top for skipping the queue, on the origin chain when depositing and on Arc when redeeming. Anything charged on Arc is taken in the claim token (bCRCL, bGLD, bUSDT, bBTCB), which is a 1:1 claim on the asset held in custody and is therefore valued as that origin asset; a fast-lane deposit is charged on the origin chain instead, before the asset becomes a claim, so it is taken in the origin token directly. Either way the fee is denominated in the same four origin assets.
definitions.revenue: All the bridge fees and the fast-lane fees go to the protocol's treasury with nothing paid out of it.

definitions.fees: Meow's own output fee (0.25% by default, lower for wallets holding the configured token), taken from each swap's output and emitted as FeeCollected. Fees charged by the underlying pools are not included.
definitions.revenue: All swap fees accrue to the Meow treasury.

definitions.fees: Creator tax on swaps of coins launched through Kicker pots (floor, launcher, buyback and platform parts) plus the 0.5% fee on pot deposits, in the pot's core asset.
definitions.revenue: The platform shares (10% of taxes on coins launched with terms and the platform part of deposit fees) plus the core that pots spend buying and burning KICKER (Burn events with KICKER as the burned token). Creator tax onto pot floors is not revenue.
definitions.holders: Core that pots spend buying and burning KICKER, counted when the burn executes (Burn event, KICKER burned, tokens > 0), from the buyback share of taxes on coins launched with KICKER as their burn target. Pot shares (K) are redeemable vault shares, not a governance or value-accrual token, so floor accrual is not holders revenue.

definitions.fees: Concentrated liquidity swap fees paid by traders. Each swap is charged on its input amount at the dynamic CLPool.fee() in effect for that swap (read from the state right before the swap's block; 3000 means 0.30%), net of any registered tx.origin discount.
definitions.revenue: Concentrated liquidity fees routed to veArchery voters through gauges, equal to HoldersRevenue.
definitions.holders: Voter fee share is measured from CLPool.gaugeFees() deltas plus CollectFees events and applied per token.

definitions.fees: Fees from the GAS/USO pool that reach Gas (95% of the swap tax and of the LP fee; Doppler keeps the other 5%), plus what players pay to buy NFT cars (in $GAS) and to repair them (in USO). The 15-minute launch sniper tax on 2026-09-23 (forwarded to a team wallet during the launch tax decay) is not counted.
definitions.revenue: All car sales and repairs, plus the 25% of pool fees sent to the buybacks wallet.
definitions.holders: Pool fees and car-sale shares sent to the buybacks wallet 0x18eD3E25Fb4786EA60021E2e9A2Da0A52602f503: 25% of pool fees, and 80% of car sales since 2026-09-23 05:59 UTC (paid in $GAS and held in that wallet). Buybacks are made by hand when the team decides and have not started yet. Before 2026-09-23 05:59 UTC the 80% car-sale share was burned.

definitions.fees: Router fee taken on the input leg of every swap through TartSwapRouterV2 (TartSwapExecuted.feeAmount, 35 bps by default, per-account custom fees possible). Excludes PancakeSwap's LP fee on the forwarded swap.
definitions.revenue: Share of the swap fee that TartFeeDistributor routes to the treasury and reserve legs, per its on-chain split() at the end of the period.

definitions.fees: 1% (100 bps) app fee charged on swaps routed through Relay, collected in USDC. Reported per origin chain of the swap.
definitions.revenue: All app fees accrue to the Based protocol; there is no supply-side or holder share.

definitions.fees: All stock- and launched-token-denominated swap charges in V1 and V2 V4 pools, including opening-period charges and caller incentives; all V2 bonding-curve trading fees and opening-window token burns; plus launch fees. Token charges are recorded in raw units and contribute to USD totals only when DefiLlama pricing supports them; missing prices leave USD coverage incomplete. Excludes strategy profits and buybacks, Uniswap LP fees, external routing fees, and Pons/$HEDGE taxes.
definitions.revenue: The designated protocol share of stock trading fees on the curve and in pools as they accrue, the creator share of launches made by the protocol recipient itself, plus launch fees; excludes royalties of other creators and launched-token strategy allocations.

definitions.fees: USDC creation fee paid by users to create an AI agent on Arc through the Fuci agent factory (1 USDC per agent at launch; read from each AgentCreated event), plus the fee on escrow jobs paid out to an agent (1% of the job at launch; read from each FuciEscrow Released event), plus Fuci Launch trading fees: the 1% Uniswap v4 LP fee on every swap in a launch pool and the snipe tax on early buys.
definitions.revenue: Creation fees, escrow fees and the Fuci Launch snipe tax (all sent to the Fuci treasury, a Safe multisig), plus Fuci Launch LP fees paid in $FUCI, which are all burned.
definitions.holders: $FUCI burned by the Fuci launchpad's collectAndBurn, which collects each launch's LP fees and burns them, usually once a day.

definitions.fees: 2% performance fee on the realised profit of each copied position, charged only on profitable closes.
definitions.revenue: The 0.8% of realised profit kept by the protocol, measured directly as USDG transfers into the treasury.

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by traders, taken from each Swap event's swapFeeAmount. The Vault charges the fee on the input token; it is booked on the same leg as the volume. When that leg is the output token (a non-core token sold for a core asset), the fee is converted at the trade's own rate, amountOut * swapFeeAmount / amountIn - no external price is used. The amount is exact; only its denomination changes. Because amountIn includes the fee itself and the trade's average rate is slightly worse than the pool's marginal rate, the converted fee reads low by about the pool's fee rate plus the trade's own price impact - a share of the fee, never of volume, and always in the under-counting direction.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of the swap fee, read per pool from the protocol fee controller.
definitions.holders: Zero - no part of the fee is distributed to token holders today.

definitions.fees: Interest paid by Alula borrowers plus operation fees on deposits, withdrawals, borrows, repayments and collateral moves.
definitions.revenue: The take rate on borrower interest (set per pool) plus operation fees, paid to the protocol and its insurance fund.

definitions.fees: Two things the trader pays. The pool fee on each swap - two of these pools run Ellipse's market-hours hook and charge 1%, 2% or 3% depending on whether the underlying market is open or shut, so for those the rate is read from the swap itself rather than assumed, and the rest are fixed at creation. Plus Ellipse's own 0.5% on swaps routed through its front end, read from the event its fee collector emits when it is emptied, which reports what actually reached the treasury rather than what was sent.
definitions.revenue: Ellipse's 0.5% interface fee, kept in full. It is charged on every swap routed through its front end, which is a wider set than the pools whose volume is reported here, so it is not 0.5% of that volume and should not be read as a rate on it. It is dated when the collector is emptied rather than when each swap paid it; a keeper does that hourly.
definitions.holders: Money going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: Acquisition fees net of quick-sell payouts, plus settlement fees, retained penalties and early crown exit fees.
definitions.revenue: Protocol's cut of fees after builder rewards, kept by the team or spent on burned FWA.
definitions.holders: FWA bought back with protocol fees and burned.

definitions.fees: The 0.25% integrator fee HyperDex charges on every swap, bridge and basket order routed through LI.FI: the FeesForwarded leg paid to HyperDex in a transaction whose LI.FI event carries integrator "hyperdex".
definitions.revenue: All of the integrator fee goes to HyperDex.

definitions.fees: Quote-asset fees and creator tax settled by Pons V2 on the $HEDGE/NVDA curve and its specific graduated pool. Uses the curve and hook sweep events, like the existing Pons V2 adapter; it does not count subsequent escrow claims or Safe transfers again.
definitions.revenue: The creatorAmount allocated to $HEDGE's fee recipient by its curve and graduated-pool sweeps. This combines the creator's share of Pons' standard fee and the creator tax; the event does not separate them. Classification of token tax as revenue is subject to DefiLlama review.

definitions.fees: Builder code fees paid by traders on free Floatout DEXes, on top of Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees collected by Floatout on free DEXes.

definitions.fees: All fees paid by traders in Synthra pools (each pool fee tier) and on Synthra Launch curves (the exact Trade fee).
definitions.revenue: Pool protocol fees, the protocol share of fees earned by launch positions locked at graduation, and the exact Launch protocol share.

definitions.fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades executed through Synthra.
definitions.revenue: Hyperliquid builder code fees collected by Synthra from perpetual trades.

definitions.fees: Application fees paid on successful Synthra router trades: Relay paidAppFees and LI.FI integrator fees.
definitions.revenue: All router application fees are collected by Synthra.

definitions.fees: The full native-USDC entry price accepted for every BoneYard NFT mint, read from Boneyard's Minted.price event. Excludes BONE genesis reserve, BONE emitted by burns, secondary royalties, and hook swap levies.
definitions.revenue: Mint fees less Charge paid to existing Skeletons. Before LP activation, the retained revenue is the project share plus protocol-owned liquidity bootstrap; after LP activation it is the project share plus BONE-buyback funding.
definitions.holders: Native USDC allocated by Hook.BuybackAccrualAdded from post-LP mints for market-buying and burning BONE, plus any pre-LP bootstrap reclassified to that reserve by BootstrapDivertedToBuyback at liquidity seeding. It is counted when funded, not when the owner executes the capped buyback. BONE is the protocol's own value-accrual token.

definitions.fees: Fees are tracked from the fee field in Swapped events, denominated in the input token. A swap is free unless its route beats the best single DEX by at least 0.1%, counted after gas; the fee is then at most 0.5% (0.05% between stablecoins; 0.15% on router v1).
definitions.revenue: All swap fees go to the Felynx treasury.

definitions.fees: Commission paid by limit-order makers (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn) plus the Uniswap v4 LP fees earned by resting order liquidity, booked when an order is settled or partially filled at creation. Amounts in other tokens are valued on the USDG side at the order band's own execution price.
definitions.revenue: All commission (2.5% of converted proceeds and of the LP fees their orders earn), paid to the TickerSpring treasury.

definitions.fees: Everything users pay through Packed: the flat 0.0004 ETH launch fee, the 1% fee on every trade on a Packed bonding curve (Robinhood Chain), the 1% LP fee of every Packed coin's Uniswap v4 pool (after graduation on Robinhood Chain, from launch on Ethereum), the creator tax a coin's creator sets at launch (0-5%, on curve trades and pool swaps), the anti-snipe charges of a coin's first seconds or first block, and the bids paid for seats in packs launched from deposits on Ethereum. All of it is paid by users: launch fees and bids by creators and pack members, the rest by traders. Pool fees are counted when they are collected from the position.
definitions.revenue: Packed's share: the launch fee in full, 25% of the 1% curve fee, 25% of the 1% pool fee, and half of every seat bid.
definitions.holders: ETH Packed spends buying back $PACKD, its own token, on the open market on Robinhood Chain, from the fee wallet and the team wallet; the coins bought are burned. It is part of Revenue, moved out of ProtocolRevenue.

definitions.fees: Total fees from Rhiva liquidity provision activity, including referral and protocol shares.
definitions.revenue: Protocol share of Rhiva fees (~90%) collected by Rhiva.

definitions.fees: V2 swap fees paid by traders, taken from each pool's Fees events, which record the exact fee charged on each swap's input amount at the fee rate in effect for that swap.
definitions.revenue: V2 swap fees routed to veArchery voters through gauges, equal to HoldersRevenue.
definitions.holders: Fees accrued to the gauge's staked LP balance, from the pool's fee index accounting: change in claimable + balanceOf(gauge) * (index - supplyIndex[gauge]) / 1e18, plus fees the gauge claimed in the period.

definitions.fees: 0.05% fee that users pay on every swap made through World by Starra, settled in USDC.
definitions.revenue: All swap fees go to the protocol.

definitions.fees: Card Wall card pack pulls paid by players, minus refunded pulls and the $WALL paid back to winners who sell their card to the house.
definitions.revenue: Card Wall card pack pulls net of refunds and card buybacks, all kept by the Card Wall team; the cost of the prize cards is paid off chain and is not deducted.

definitions.fees: USDC paid to launch a token, the 0.1% fee on public USDC committed during a guarded opening, and USDC-side Uniswap v3 LP fees generated by permanently locked Souless launch positions and collected on-chain.
definitions.revenue: The protocol-retained share of launch and collected LP fees, all guarded-opening fees, and any unallocated Launch Partner campaign remainder returned to the protocol by the LaunchPartnerPool. LP-fee revenue is the residual after creator, Community, actual active-partner, and active-referrer allocations.

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by users at each pool's fee tier, in the token each swap paid in, plus the arbitrage profit of the protocol's satellite pools.
definitions.revenue: The protocol fee (each pool's share of the swap fee, read from the pool: 1/4 on every pool since launch), the LP fees earned by protocol-owned liquidity, and all satellite arbitrage profit.
definitions.holders: Half of the protocol fee and 12.5% of satellite arbitrage profit, sent to a fee jar that auctions it for GOO and burns the GOO.

definitions.fees: Bonding-curve trading fees (1%, plus the snipe tax on buys in the first seconds after launch), creators' own taxes on curve trades, swap fees in graduated coins' Uniswap V3 pools, the ETH launch fee, the trade router's 0.05% fee on every trade sent from the site, and the protocol's share of every front-page bid: 25% of a bid on a coin launched here, all of a bid on a coin launched on PONS. A reward coin's transfer fee, a token tax paid in the launched coin, is not counted.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of trading fees and of the swap fees earned by locked graduation liquidity (each coin's immutable protocolShareBps, 30% at launch), launch fees, the trade router's fee, and the buyback and treasury shares of bids.

definitions.fees: Total swap fees paid by traders on Biatec's Algorand pools, from Biatec's own trade indexer (AVM Trade Reporter).
definitions.revenue: Portion of swap fees kept by the Biatec protocol.

definitions.fees: Protocol fees from all visible Haedal lending vaults on that completed UTC day. Depositor yield is not included.
definitions.revenue: The same protocol fees, as reported in the endpoint's revenue field.

definitions.fees: Assessment fees paid in USDC.
definitions.revenue: Assessment fees minus trader payouts and referral and affiliate commissions.

definitions.fees: The router fee (1 basis point of the output amount) paid by users on every swap.
definitions.revenue: All router fees go to the vfat.io fee collector.

definitions.fees: 0.05% of the amount traded, collected by TRDEFI on positions created through its venue. The fee is embedded in the maker's signed order and paid to the receiver address when the position trades, so it is counted as the incoming token transfers it actually is. The fee rail has been in force since 2026-09-25; positions created before that carry no fee and are immutable.
definitions.revenue: The entire collected trading fee. TRDEFI retains 100% of it, with no share paid to suppliers or holders.

definitions.fees: Native-token fees paid by users for completed Primus verification reports.
definitions.revenue: The portion of verification fees paid to Primus.

definitions.fees: Launch fees, the 1% fee on curve trades, the 1% hook fee on swaps in graduated pools (all from the contracts' fee-accrual events), and the swap fee on frenlaunch's Doppler pools (ten times the platform's 10% integrator payout).
definitions.revenue: All launch fees, the platform's 25% of curve and graduated-pool trading fees, the platform's 10% integrator share of Doppler pool swap fees, and the 10% referrer seat on Doppler pools launched without a referrer (the platform holds that seat).

definitions.fees: Everything users pay: the fee charged on each swap of a launched token, the higher fee charged in the first minutes after a launch, the fee to create a launch, and the fee the Peddles Terminal and trade bot add to a swap.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of each swap fee and of the opening fee, plus all launch fees and all Terminal and trade bot fees.

definitions.fees: Positive perpetual trading fees plus builder surcharges paid by users. Excludes funding payments and spot.
definitions.revenue: Fees minus supply-side revenue. Because rebates and the MegaPop contribution accrue on their own rules, this is negative when they exceed fees collected in the window.
definitions.holders: PopDEX does not buy back, burn, or distribute fees to token holders, so this is zero.

definitions.fees: All launch fees, bonding-curve trading fees and graduated-pool hook fees, counted when the curve or the hook distributes them.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of trading fees plus the launch fees in full.

definitions.fees: Trading fees on FAZE bonding curves and graduated pools, plus token launch and graduation fees. Settled fees are adjusted for opening and closing pending balances.
definitions.revenue: Fees retained by FAZE: platform treasury allocations plus creator fees from FAZE own-token pools. Excludes other projects creator allocations and fees allocated to locked liquidity. Buybacks are a subsequent capital allocation, not additional revenue.
definitions.holders: Native USDC fees paid by the hook to the designated FAZE buyback burner, less failed-payment recredits and actual keeper rewards. Recognized at funding rather than swap execution; excludes unrelated deposits and other tokens burners.

definitions.fees: A 1% fee on every Loong trade, on the bonding curve and in graduated PancakeSwap Infinity pools (charged by the Loong hook), plus the launch-window anti-snipe tax (starts at 99% and decays to 0 over 3 seconds) and any token creation fee (currently 0).
definitions.revenue: The 0.10% platform share and the 0.10% $LOONG buyback-and-burn share of every trade, plus token creation fees.
definitions.holders: The 0.10% of every trade that funds $LOONG buybacks and burns; on the $LOONG coin itself its own 0.10% coin buyback-and-burn share also buys $LOONG.

definitions.fees: Builder-code fees paid by users trading Hyperliquid perps through the Kinetiq Markets interface.
definitions.revenue: Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid perps trades, retained entirely by Kinetiq.

definitions.fees: The app's 0.1% interface fee on its Nordstern routes (Nordstern encodes it in 1/65536 steps, so 0.0992%), taken from each trade's output. Fees paid in GOO are valued at the trade's own price.
definitions.revenue: All interface fees go to the Goo Exchange treasury.

definitions.fees: Swap fees estimated from each pool's configured fee tier and one token side of each swap. Excludes V2.5 pools.
Jumper platform fees (0-5 bps depending on the assets) paid by users on bridges.
definitions.revenue: All platform fees are kept by Jumper.

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by users
Builder code fees paid by users trading Hyperliquid perpetuals through Jumper.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees attributed to Jumper from Hyperliquid perpetual trades.

definitions.fees: Every bonding curve trade pays 1.20%: a 0.70% protocol fee to Motoswap and a 0.50% fee to the coin creator.
definitions.revenue: The whole 0.70% protocol fee: the shares for MOTO stakers, MOTO buyback and burn, the treasury and the Rakeback program.
definitions.holders: The share of the 0.70% protocol fee paid to MOTO stakers plus the share used to buy back and burn MOTO.

definitions.fees: Builder code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid perpetual trades placed through DXAP (0.1% until 2026-07-09, 0.01% until 2026-09-03, 0.025% since); excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees collected by DXAP from Hyperliquid perpetual trades.

definitions.fees: 1% of every trade on the bonding curve and in the graduated Uniswap v4 pools, plus the flat USDC fee paid to launch a coin.
definitions.revenue: 30% of every trading fee and every launch fee, sent to the Lockcurve treasury.

definitions.fees: Builder Fees collected from Orderly Network
definitions.revenue: All the fees collected

definitions.fees: ORBIO creator and LP fees collected in harvests plus CREDIT order-book buyer fees swept by staking, excluding CREDIT activation burns and launchpad ORBIO fees.
definitions.revenue: Harvest and order-book fees allocated to treasury and ORBIO token holders.
definitions.holders: The harvest share allocated as inference backing to ORBIO stakers, valued in USDG when funded rather than when claimed.

definitions.fees: Two things, and they are different money, and only the first of them is paid by anyone: it is reported as the user fee as well. First, the fee a trader paid on a swap in a pool the plugin runs in, at the rate the plugin set for that swap; the plugin takes no share of that fee, so nothing of it is charged to the user on the protocol's behalf. Second, the arbitrage the plugin realised inside the pool and paid out, read from the ProfitDistributed event where a deployment settles through a distributor and from the donatedToLps leg of ProfitShared where the plugin pays the pool's liquidity providers directly.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of the captured arbitrage, taken from the distributor's own share config as it stood at the block of each capture. Nothing of the swap fee is the protocol's, and the captures donated straight to liquidity providers leave it nothing either.

definitions.fees: All yield generated by Arrowfarm concentrated liquidity vaults: LP trading fees and gauge rewards harvested by the strategies, the performance fee charged on them, and trading fees sent straight to the treasury.
definitions.revenue: Performance fees charged on harvests (arrow fee and strategist fee, paid in WETH) plus trading fees that strategies send to the treasury. The harvest caller fee is not counted as revenue.
definitions.holders: The arrow performance fee in WETH is sent to the ArrowBuybackBurner, which buys ARROWFARM and burns it.

definitions.fees: Platform fees paid by GDEX users. Solana: received in SOL by the GDEX treasury, 1% of the SOL side of each swap and 0.1% on SOL withdrawals (1% when bridging). EVM chains: the 1% swap fee paid to the GDEX treasury by the KyberSwap router GDEX routes swaps through; EVM transfer and bridge fees are not included.
Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through GDEX.
definitions.revenue: Hyperliquid builder code fees collected by GDEX. Referral rewards GDEX later pays out off-chain from its treasury are not deducted.

definitions.fees: Builder code fees paid on trades routed through Hypercall; excludes Hyperliquid trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees collected by Hypercall on those trades.

definitions.fees: The total trading fees paid by users, excluding L1 transaction fees. Only the 50 largest SundaeSwap pools by current TVL (across all versions) are counted, and the same current set is used for past dates, so pools that were large in the past but are not in today's top 50 are excluded.
definitions.revenue: A fixed ADA cost per transaction that is collected by the protocol. Only the 50 largest SundaeSwap pools by current TVL (across all versions) are counted, and the same current set is used for past dates, so pools that were large in the past but are not in today's top 50 are excluded.
definitions.holders: The share of the fixed ADA cost per transaction going to holders: 15% since May 2024, 0% before. Only the 50 largest SundaeSwap pools by current TVL (across all versions) are counted, and the same current set is used for past dates, so pools that were large in the past but are not in today's top 50 are excluded.

definitions.fees: Every trade pays the pair swap fee (0.30%) to liquidity providers, a 0.70% Motoswap protocol fee on the quote side, and on coins that graduated from moto.fun a 0.30% creator fee.
definitions.revenue: The whole 0.70% protocol fee: the shares for MOTO stakers, MOTO buyback and burn, the treasury and the Rakeback program.
definitions.holders: The share of the 0.70% protocol fee paid to MOTO stakers plus the share used to buy back and burn MOTO.

definitions.fees: Everything traders pay on a swap: the pool's swap fee from the Swap event (protocol fee included), plus what a Latch launch pool's guard takes itself - the creator tax, and on newer launch guards the guard's part of the trade fee - read from the guard's TaxTaken and FeeTaken events. Only Latch's own launch guards are read.
definitions.revenue: What reaches the protocol, counted when the fee is taken: the protocol fee each Swap event carries; the protocol's share of a launch pool's liquidity fees under the pool's permanent LP lock split, only where the locks provably hold all of the pool's liquidity; and the protocol's share of the creator tax and guard trade fee under the split the guard stores for that pool. A split that cannot be read is never guessed: that amount is left out of Revenue.

definitions.fees: Aerodrome LP fees distributed to MAMO stakers.
definitions.revenue: Aerodrome LP fees distributed to MAMO stakers.
definitions.holders: Aerodrome LP trading fees distributed to MAMO stakers via the multi-rewards contract.

definitions.fees: Integrator fee TRNCH adds to swaps and bridges made on TRNCH (0.5% on a single swap, 1% on a swap of a token from the TRNCH Heat ranking or on a basket of swaps, 1% on bridges, 0.5% on swaps built through the TRNCH Bot API and MCP server for AI agents), paid to the TRNCH treasury Safe through LI.FI, KyberSwap, 0x, Uniswap, SushiSwap and 1inch. Router and DEX fees are excluded.
definitions.revenue: All integrator fees received by the TRNCH treasury Safe are kept by TRNCH.

definitions.fees: All swap fees paid by traders on ADEXTO bonding curves, read from each Swap event: the creator, curve reserve, buyback and protocol legs. Rates are set per market at launch and never change; the launch presets are 1.00% on factory 1.0.0 and 0.12.0 markets and 0.40% on factory 0.11.0 markets.
definitions.revenue: The protocol leg of every swap, paid to the ADEXTO protocol treasury: 0.10% of the trade on factory 0.11.0, 0.12.0 and 1.0.0 markets, where it is a factory constant. Factory 0.10.0 markets have no protocol leg.

definitions.fees: Borrow origination, repayment and explicit liquidation fees, and lending entry and exit fees, valued in USD when charged.
definitions.revenue: All of the fees (Borrow, Repay, Deposit, Withdraw); the protocol keeps them in full.

definitions.fees: Carriers pay XNET for mobile data offloaded onto WiFi. Until settlement arrives, Fees are conservatively accrued from measured daily offload. Closed unsettled months use XNET's official monthly projection and newer days use a conservative API-GB rate. Carrier payments typically settle about two months later, and historical accrual is reconciled to the amount actually paid.
definitions.revenue: Carriers pay XNET for mobile data offloaded onto WiFi. Until settlement arrives, Fees are conservatively accrued from measured daily offload. Closed unsettled months use XNET's official monthly projection and newer days use a conservative API-GB rate. Carrier payments typically settle about two months later, and historical accrual is reconciled to the amount actually paid.
definitions.holders: Accrued service-period tokenholder allocation. Historically 80% of ordinary carrier Fees accrued to buyback-and-burn; under passed XIP-12, 60% does. The XIP-13.1 fiat slice contributes its 5% facilitation/BBB allocation. Values are provisional wherever the underlying Fees are provisional and reconcile with settlement. This is accrual attribution; actual on-chain buyback or burn execution can occur later.

definitions.fees: Builder fees received by crotrade from trades on Polymarket v2
definitions.revenue: Builder fees received by crotrade from trades on Polymarket v2
definitions.holders: Builder fees received by crotrade, all distributed to its token holders

definitions.fees: Every trading fee cro.trade users pay on spot trades routed through cro.trade's contracts on Cronos, measured from the fee each trade pays on-chain. Trades whose fee leaves no on-chain event are not included, so the figure is a floor.
definitions.revenue: All trading fees; no share goes to liquidity providers.
definitions.holders: All trading fees go to CRONUS holders through buybacks: distributed to holders before 2026-09-22, burned since.

definitions.fees: Actual quote-asset swap charges emitted by the verified TaxHook FeesAccrued event. V1 launches charge no trading tax. No token mint allocation, gas, deposits, claim payments or buyback execution is counted as a new fee.
definitions.revenue: Treasury allocation of each fee on an accrual basis; excludes creators, referrers and launched-token buybacks.

definitions.fees: Bridge fees paid by users on completed transfers.
definitions.revenue: Bridge fees retained by LilSwap after partner share.

definitions.fees: Yield from RealFi's reserve portfolio (treasury bills, money market funds, CLO ETFs, floating-rate bonds and private credit), counted when it is minted on-chain as new USDrf at each weekly staking epoch, net of portfolio losses burned from the sUSDrf staking vault. Excludes income RealFi earns off-chain on unstaked USDrf reserves that is never minted on-chain. Mint and redeem fees are currently 0 bps.
definitions.revenue: Share of each epoch's minted yield sent to the RealFi protocol fee address instead of the sUSDrf staking vault.

definitions.fees: ZC burned by users to publish in the Book, relay fees on private posts, payments and withdrawals, and deposit vetting fees of the ZC privacy pool. The launcher share of Stockereum's swap fee on ZC trades is a token tax and is not counted.
definitions.revenue: All fees: burns accrue to holders, the rest to the protocol; no supply-side payments except relay fees earned by third-party relayers.
definitions.holders: ZC permanently burned by users to post.

definitions.fees: Escrow fees paid by sellers and buyers on completed P2P trades, read from EscrowComplete events. Fees are tiered by trade size (fixed fee below 50 USD, then 1.25% down to 0.25%) with a lower rate for verified merchants. Cancelled or refunded trades pay no fee.
definitions.revenue: All escrow fees are kept by the protocol.

definitions.fees: Everything PeddleQuest charges: the fee quest creators pay on top of the reward pool they deposit, the flat quest creation fee, the protocol's share of rewards that winners did not claim before the deadline, payments for trending and banner promotion slots, and the fee users pay to mint an optional completion badge.
definitions.revenue: All fees (quest creation, deposit, unclaimed, promotion and badge) are kept by the protocol. Quest rewards themselves go to winners and are not counted as fees or revenue.
definitions.holders: The share of badge mint fees routed on-chain to buyback and burn. Zero while that route is switched off, which it has been since launch.

definitions.fees: 0.5% protocol fee on shielded pool deposits and 0.5% on withdrawals (Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Solana), deposit check fees on Solana, plus ZEC rewards received by the Nullmask team wallet from MASK token holder distributions (Solana).
definitions.revenue: 0.5% protocol fee on shielded pool deposits and 0.5% on withdrawals (Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Robinhood Chain, Solana), deposit check fees on Solana, plus ZEC rewards received by the Nullmask team wallet from MASK token holder distributions (Solana).

definitions.fees: Lock creation fees paid by users to Titan Locker, read from FeeCollected events on every lock manager: a flat ETH fee, or a share of the deposited token for ERC-20 and vesting locks.
definitions.revenue: All lock creation fees go to the Titan Locker fee receiver.
definitions.holders: Titan Locker has no token, so no fees go to token holders.

definitions.fees: Copy trading fees fomo-mcp users pay on every copied buy and sell (1% on copies under $100, 0.5% from $100), plus the creator fees of the fomo-mcp token $FOMOMCP on the Pons launchpad.
definitions.revenue: All fees (copy trading fees and $FOMOMCP creator fees) are kept by fomo-mcp.

definitions.fees: Bonding-curve fee paid in the native token on every launchpad buy and sell.
definitions.revenue: Launchpad fee kept by Crystal after the token creator's split.

definitions.fees: USDW trading fees accrued to the protocol, measured as the increase in FeeRouter.totalPlatformFees() on each chain where Wager Predict is deployed.
definitions.revenue: The same increase in FeeRouter.totalPlatformFees(). That counter is the platform's collected trading fees.

definitions.fees: Fees charged on bets in every V5, V6 and V7 room: the room stakers' fee (V5 / V6), the platform fee and the room creator's fee.
definitions.revenue: The platform fee on bets, sent to the ElcasTreasury (V5) or the ElcasBurner (V6, V7).
definitions.holders: The ElcasTreasury / ElcasBurner swaps the platform fee to $ELCAS and burns it.

definitions.fees: Open and close fees (a share of the position size, set per market) and hourly borrow paid by traders.
definitions.revenue: The platform's share of open and close fees (currently 10 %), accrued for the platform's fee address.
definitions.holders: Fees going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: The fee taken from each settled round's losing side (set per market, up to 6 %).
definitions.revenue: The platform's share of each round's fee (currently 1 % of the losing side).

definitions.fees: Platform fees, integrator app fees and swap costs paid by users on Relay bridges and swaps, excluding execution costs (network gas).
definitions.revenue: Platform fees. This is an upper bound: Relay pays qualifying integrators an undisclosed 0-67% revenue share out of it.

definitions.fees: Fees paid on room-key buys and sells, the flat fee to launch a room token, and swap fees earned by room-token liquidity. Excludes fees on Spot swaps routed through third-party aggregators.
definitions.revenue: AlfaClub's platform key-trading fee, room-token launch fees and 15% of room-token swap fees, plus the creator shares in AlfaClub's own room, the room behind the ALFA token.

definitions.fees: Pons creator fees paid to Mosh bundles (each bundle's swarm contract), plus the one-time raise fee Mosh takes when a bundle launches. The creator fees are also counted by Pons V2 as its creators' share, so this adapter is marked as double counted.
definitions.revenue: Mosh's share of the creator fees (creatorFeeShareBps, 20% at launch), the raise fee (raiseFeeBps, 5% of the filled raise), and, where the Mosh treasury holds a bundle's fee claims itself, its pro-rata part of the backers' share.

definitions.fees: Trading fees and builder fees paid on Derive perpetual trades.
definitions.revenue: Trading fees minus maker rebates.
definitions.holders: Fees going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: Trading fees and builder fees paid on Derive options trades.
definitions.revenue: Trading fees minus maker rebates.
definitions.holders: DRV bought back with a share of fees from all Derive markets (options, perps and spot), held by the Derive DAO treasury.

definitions.fees: Trading fees and builder fees paid on Derive spot trades.
definitions.revenue: Trading fees minus maker rebates.
definitions.holders: Money going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by users.
definitions.revenue: SunSwap V4 charges no protocol fee, so the protocol keeps no revenue.

definitions.fees: Builder-code fees paid by users trading Hyperliquid spot through the Kinetiq Markets interface.
definitions.revenue: Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid spot trades, retained entirely by Kinetiq.

definitions.fees: Fees users pay when closing or settling HIP-4 outcome positions, including builder-code fees added by front-ends. Hyperliquid charged no outcome fee of its own before 15 Aug 2026.
definitions.revenue: 99% of outcome fees net of builder-code fees, sent to the Assistance Fund to buy HYPE.
definitions.holders: 99% of outcome fees net of builder-code fees, used by the Assistance Fund to buy back HYPE.
