definitions.fees: 2% fee on realized PnL at close, 2% fee on margin lost in liquidations, and LP profits above the $5M cap swept to PAPER stakers. Trader wins and losses that stay in the LP are not counted.
definitions.revenue: All fees: half of the 2% fees to PAPER stakers, half to the dev fee recipient, and LP profits above the $5M cap to PAPER stakers.
definitions.holders: Half of the 2% close and liquidation fees plus LP profits above the $5M cap, paid in USDC to PAPER stakers.

definitions.fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on trades placed through Auspex; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees collected by Auspex. Referral rewards Auspex later pays out from its treasury are not deducted.

definitions.fees: Open and close fees (a share of the position size, set per market) and hourly borrow paid by traders.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of open and close fees (currently 10 %), collected in the protocol's FeeVault.
definitions.holders: Fees going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: Swap fee charged on the output token of each swap (protocol share plus LP share), read from the Swapped event. The coverage toll a swap may pay when it drains a leg below its coverage floor stays in the leg's reserves as a buffer and is not counted.
definitions.revenue: Protocol share (protoFee) of the swap fee. Zero on coop fills, which book no protocol fee.

definitions.fees: SOL service fees paid by users to Tsunammi for the Create Token flow.
definitions.revenue: All tracked Create Token service fees are retained as Tsunammi protocol revenue.

definitions.fees: Everything traders pay on the bonding curves of tokens launched with Ryntra Launch (Meteora DBC pools on its configs, created by its pool payer), including the 20% Meteora keeps; after graduation, the referral fee Meteora pays Ryntra on trades made through Ryntra; and what Ryntra takes as the partner of a graduated curve (its share of the migration fee, and later the fees of the DAMM v2 liquidity locked for it) when its fee claimer withdraws them. The creator's share of the migration fee and the quote above the graduation threshold (not a fee) are not included.
definitions.revenue: Ryntra's 60% of the configs' share of the bonding curve fee, the referral fees Meteora pays it, and its graduation income when withdrawn.

definitions.fees: Fees people pay Ryntra on trades made through it. On Solana: what the swap router (Jupiter, or DFlow when Jupiter routes through it) pays into Ryntra's fee wallet and its Jupiter referral account inside the trade. On Arc: the developer fee of a Circle swap and the fee leg of a KyberSwap swap that name Ryntra's fee address, read from Circle's fee collector and KyberSwap's router events. Plain transfers into these accounts are not fees.
definitions.revenue: Trading fees kept by Ryntra: the whole fee paid into its fee wallet on Solana and from KyberSwap on Arc, what reached its Jupiter referral account less Jupiter's 20% share, and the Circle developer fee less the share (about 10%) Circle's fee collector routes to its protocol recipient. Cashback and invite rewards are paid later, when people claim them, and are not deducted.

definitions.fees: Commission SX Bet takes on the profit of winning bets, counted when the escrow pays it to SX's fee wallet at settlement. On V3 the rates are set per account and can apply to singles as well as parlays; losing and voided bets pay nothing.
definitions.revenue: Commission taken from the profit of winning bets and kept by SX. Market makers get none of it.

definitions.fees: Everything charged on the launchpad: DEEP's fee on each bonding-curve buy and sell (1.25%), the reward fee a token's creator chose at launch (0% to 5% of each trade), the fee to launch a token ($2, paid in SOL) and the migration fee taken from the SOL a curve raised when its token graduates (1%, less the network rent of the new pool's accounts).
definitions.revenue: DEEP's share: its 1.25% fee on bonding-curve trades, the token launch fees and the migration fees. Reward fees are not included.

definitions.fees: Everything charged on DeepSwap: the swap fee (0.35% of a buy and 0.75% of a sell), the reward fee the pool charges on top of it (0% to 5%, fixed when the pool was created) and the flat fee in SOL to open a pool. Pools of graduated launchpad tokens are opened by the launchpad, which pays that fee out of the token's migration fee; it is reported with the launchpad, not here.
definitions.revenue: DEEP's share of the swap fee (0.25% of a buy, 0.65% of a sell) and the pool creation fees.
definitions.holders: Money going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by users
definitions.revenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury and/or token holders
definitions.holders: Money going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by users
definitions.revenue: Percentage of swap fees going to treasury and/or token holders
definitions.holders: Money going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: QUOTUM trading tax collected by TaxSink, measured in NVDA when claimed, excluding Pons platform fees and direct funding transfers.
definitions.revenue: Claimed QUOTUM trading tax less cash NVDA forwarded to PAY_TO, including backing funding, with claims and transfers recognized when executed; retained funding and later buybacks can make attribution differ within a period.
definitions.holders: NVDA spent on successful QUOTUM buybacks and burns at the daily bell, excluding failed purchases and direct token burns.

definitions.fees: Trading fees paid by users on every Vaultex coin: 2% of each buy and sell on the bonding curve, in the coin's quote asset (SOL, USDC and more), read from Meteora DBC swap events. Most of it goes to the coin creator, split by the creator percentage of each Vaultex pool config (DBC create-config event).
definitions.revenue: Vaultex's share of the trading fee on every bonding-curve trade, claimed into the Vaultex treasury.

definitions.fees: The 0.5% fee users pay on every swap made through Monolith Exchange, collected by Jupiter into Monolith's referral fee accounts.
definitions.revenue: The 80% of the 0.5% swap fee that Monolith Exchange keeps after Jupiter's 20% share.

definitions.fees: On repayment, 3% of principal is paid to the funder and 1% of principal is paid to the protocol. The principal returned to the funder is not a fee.
definitions.revenue: The 1% protocol fee paid to the protocol address on repayment.

definitions.fees: BOT paid by consumers to request AI inference, plus forfeited dispute bonds. Inference fees are counted when a request is fulfilled - timed-out requests refund in full, so escrowed-only requests are excluded.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share (protocolFeeBps, currently 10%) of each fulfilled inference fee, plus forfeited challenge bonds, accrued to the treasury.

definitions.fees: Swap fees charged by DeepCore pools, read from each Swap event (protocol fee included), plus the fee DeepCore's router charges on fills it routes to other venues, read from its Filled events. Launch-pool creator taxes and launch-guard trade fees are not counted.
definitions.revenue: The protocol fee slice each Swap event carried, plus the router fee on routed fills. Both are paid to the protocol.

definitions.fees: Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players: refunds of cancelled pulls, card cash-outs, sell-backs, USDC prizes and reimbursed card shipments. This is the 10% fee Raflux keeps when a card is exchanged for USDC plus the game result of pulls, so it is negative on days when players win more than they pay.
definitions.revenue: Pack purchases minus USDC returned to players, kept by Raflux. No share goes to LPs, referrers or token holders.

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by traders on every swap.
definitions.revenue: Protocol share of swap fees, read per pool from the vault (protocol swap fee set by the protocol fee controller).

definitions.fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through Kokoah; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees collected by Kokoah. Referral rewards Kokoah later pays out off-chain from these fees are not deducted.

definitions.fees: The desk's fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells (20% at launch), fixed at the sale and recognized one hour later when the Safe can no longer void the sale; a voided sale charges no fee. The premium itself is not counted as fees: it is the buyer's payment for the option, which depositors carry against the risk of the call settling in the money (see the options adapter's premium volume). A call sold outside the desk (not possible with the current operator) counts the fee the operator reports at settlement.
definitions.revenue: All of the desk fee on the gross premium of each weekly call the vault sells, paid to the HedgeHood treasury Safe at settlement.

definitions.fees: On-chain BUY fee from FillEvent (SELLs and settlements are fee-free).
definitions.revenue: 100% protocol revenue — no LPs, no token, no revenue share.

definitions.fees: Trading fees paid on sprout.fun bonding curves (1% or 3% per launch) and in the Choice v2 pools that launches graduate into (same rate, taken by the Sprout hook).
definitions.revenue: Trading fees minus the share credited to launch creators and referrers (the platform share).
definitions.holders: 80% of the platform share funds SPROUT buyback and burn (ratio taken from the Sprout docs).

definitions.fees: Each swap pays a 0.25% fee.
definitions.revenue: 1/6 of swap fees (~0.0417%) accrue to the protocol via the factory feeTo LP mint.

definitions.fees: Builder code revenue from Hyperliquid Perps Trades.
definitions.revenue: Builder code revenue from Hyperliquid Perps Trades.

definitions.fees: The service fee copypump charges on every copied buy and sell, collected as a USDC transfer to the copypump treasury and counted on the day it is collected (the collector batches fees per user, so a fee can land the day after its trade).
definitions.revenue: Fees minus the fee payer cost: what copypump keeps. The 'app revenue, after gas' figure on copypumpfun.com/data.

definitions.fees: 1% swap fees on Pumper-launched tokens' Uniswap V3 pools and on the PUMPER pools, plus creator-set buy/sell taxes and the V4 hook / Lock-curve fees (1% base fee + tax) on Pumper-launched tokens. Launched tokens are taken from PumperProtocolRegistry.
definitions.revenue: 15% of every launched token's fees and taxes: 10% to adminVault and 5% to the PUMPER buy-and-burn vault. PUMPER's own pool fees carry no protocol cut.
definitions.holders: The 5% of launched token fees and taxes sent to the PUMPER buy-and-burn vault, which buys and burns PUMPER.

definitions.fees: Service fees charged by Polycool on every Polymarket buy and sell routed through the app (1.00% of the notional for new users, decreasing with lifetime volume to 0.50% above $100K, pulled from the trader's wallet into the Polycool treasury as USDC.e or pUSD), plus the Polymarket builder fees on those trades, which the trader pays inside Polymarket's trade fee and Polymarket pays out to Polycool daily.
definitions.revenue: Service fees and Polymarket builder fees, minus referral rewards paid out. No liquidity providers.

definitions.fees: The 1% bonding curve trading fee on every Ferzan coin before it graduates (Meteora's DBC fee on Solana, including Meteora's protocol share).
definitions.revenue: Ferzan's share of the curve fee: 50%, less 10% to a referrer when one is set. On Solana, half of the DBC trading fee.

definitions.fees: Fees paid by traders of coins launched on Incognito Launchpad (Solana): the launchpad's 0.25% platform fee and the coin creator's 0.5% fee on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a coin graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Key the launchpad holds. Raydium's own protocol fee is excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token.
definitions.revenue: The platform fee and the harvested locked-liquidity fees, both received by the launchpad treasury.

definitions.fees: Actual Hyperliquid builder fees paid on Ditto-routed perpetual trades; excludes venue trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder fees collected by Ditto on its routed perpetual trades.

definitions.fees: Builder-code fees paid by users on Hyperliquid spot trades placed through the builder code.
definitions.revenue: Builder-code fees on Hyperliquid spot trades, all kept by the builder.

definitions.fees: SOL paid to Peep by its users: the 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token made in Peep. Swaps between SOL and USDC/USDT, token-to-token swaps and tips carry no Peep fee. Peep's 5% share of paid group joins is not counted: a group join carries no on-chain marker that tells it apart from any transaction with the same two transfers.
definitions.revenue: SOL kept by Peep: the whole 0.75% fee on swaps between SOL and a token.

definitions.fees: Every fee traders pay on trades on the Bordrless DEX, including launched coins after they graduate: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
definitions.revenue: The protocol fee, paid to the Bordrless treasury: half is kept, half buys back $BORDR.
definitions.holders: Half of the protocol fee, spent buying back $BORDR.

definitions.fees: Every fee traders pay on trades on the Bordrless launchpad bonding curve, before a coin graduates: the protocol fee, LP fee, coin creator fee and holder reward fee.
definitions.revenue: The protocol fee, paid to the Bordrless treasury: half is kept, half buys back $BORDR.
definitions.holders: Half of the protocol fee, spent buying back $BORDR.

definitions.fees: Creator trading fees that Pons pays to Credence vaults for the tokens Credence deployed, creator fees paid into creator vaults for X accounts, and the Credence fee charged on every launch.
definitions.revenue: What Credence keeps: 20% of each token vault's creator fees, which buys back and burns $PFWA, the protocol's cut of creator vault fees, and launch fees.
definitions.holders: The 20% of each token vault's creator fees that is spent buying $PFWA sent to the dead address, counted when the fees are collected.

definitions.fees: Everything traders and market creators pay on PFWA Markets: the trading fee on buys and on sells after a market's deadline, the early-sell penalty on sells before the deadline, and the fee to create a market. Activity of PFWA's own wallets (team, market seeder, market-making agent) is excluded.
definitions.revenue: The protocol's share of all fees: the protocol's leg of every trading fee (both legs on markets the protocol created), half of every early-sell penalty, and the market creation fee, including the part spent buying back and burning $PFWA.
definitions.holders: ETH spent buying $PFWA that is burned: half of each v2 market creation fee is swapped for $PFWA in the same transaction and sent to the dead address.

definitions.fees: The 5% of the ETH side of every swap in a Sherwood game pool that is paid into the round's prize pot. Direct deposits into the pots are not fees and are excluded.
definitions.revenue: The share of the pot fees that buys back and burns $PFWA: 10% in Season 1 (ETH/$PFWA pool) and 7% in Season 2 (ETH/$IMD pool) of what is left after the Dice randomness fees.
definitions.holders: The share of the pot fees spent buying back and burning $PFWA (10% in Season 1, 7% in Season 2, after Dice randomness fees), counted when the swap pays the fee. Burns funded by direct pot deposits are excluded.

definitions.fees: Fees paid by traders on MoveFast launchpad pools: the platform trading fee, any pool fee, and the token tax each launch's creator sets. The part of the tax that burns the launched token is not included.
definitions.revenue: The platform trading fee on every MoveFast trade (1.5% of the trade), sent to the MoveFast treasury.

definitions.fees: Settled yield from mxBTC's HyperCore funding strategy after borrowing and trading costs, converted to UBTC and measured at distribution, plus instant redeem/unstake fees; excludes unsettled strategy income.
definitions.revenue: The foundation's share of settled mxBTC yield plus instant redeem/unstake fees, valued in UBTC.

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by traders on Choice v1 pools, which is 0.3% of the swap output.
definitions.revenue: One sixth of each swap fee, kept by the protocol in the Choice treasury multisig.
definitions.holders: Money going to governance token holders

definitions.fees: The 1% fee the Feast hook takes on every buy and sell of a Feast coin, paid in the coin's quote asset (a Binance tokenized stock or BNB). Excludes the PancakeSwap Infinity LP fee and the one-off 1% fee on the FEAST token sale.
definitions.revenue: The 20% platform share of every fee, plus the self-burn and creator shares of fees in the FEAST/BNB pool, all of which are used to buy and burn the FEAST platform token.
definitions.holders: The 20% platform share of every fee, sold by the platform sink for FEAST which is burned, plus the self-burn and creator shares of fees in the FEAST/BNB pool, which buy and burn FEAST.

definitions.fees: The 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base for services on Central City's Feed (other payments carry no fee), charged by Central City's immutable fee routers and sent straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.
definitions.revenue: The full 10% protocol fee on qualifying Feed service payments, which AI agents make in USDC on Base for services on Central City's Feed, kept by Central City: the immutable fee routers send it straight to the Central City treasury. Includes payments made by all agents created on Central City, counted under the same rules.

definitions.fees: Relay fees paid by users on private withdrawals, transfers and holder exits (30 bps plus a fixed gas quote), and the immutable 30 bps service fee on private swaps through the fee route adapters. Ragequit is free.
definitions.revenue: All Relay fees. Lincoln has no liquidity providers or token holders sharing fees.

definitions.fees: Fees charged when positions settle: a 0.5 basis point close charge on the order value plus the market fee (currently 2%) on the gain of winning trades and on the loss of losing and liquidated trades. Opening a position is free and there are no funding payments.
definitions.revenue: All settlement fees, split between the protocol and CARDBOARD stakers.
definitions.holders: Half of settlement fees, distributed in USDC to CARDBOARD stakers. Referral bonuses are paid from the same budget and are not separated.

definitions.fees: Profit fee of 2% on the gain of every winning trade, taken from the payout. Opening a position, losing trades and liquidations are free and there is no funding. The house bankroll's trading profit is not counted.
definitions.revenue: All profit fees, kept by Jupiter in a fee balance of the YOLO program separate from the house bankroll; there are no liquidity providers.
definitions.holders: Half of profit fees, used to buy back JUP under Jupiter's policy of spending 50% of revenue on JUP buybacks.

definitions.fees: USDC players pay to open card packs, net of refunds and instant buybacks of won cards, plus marketplace fees on card trades.
definitions.revenue: Pack sales net of refunds and buybacks, minus payouts to third-party card stakers, referral commissions and draw fees sent to the Jackpot, plus marketplace fees. Payouts for cards staked by the platform's own wallets stay in revenue.

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by traders, at the dynamic fee the Nami plugin sets for each swap.
definitions.revenue: Swap fees of gauged pools, paid to Nami token holders: 90% to veNAMI voters and 10% to ogNAMI stakers.
definitions.holders: Swap fees of gauged pools paid to veNAMI voters (90%) and ogNAMI stakers (10%).

definitions.fees: Builder fees paid by users on perps trades routed through HypurrTrade (0.05% until 2026-10-08, 0.1% since); excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder fees collected by HypurrTrade from Hyperliquid perps trades.

definitions.fees: Users pay each pool's configured fee tier (0.01% to 5%) on every swap.
definitions.revenue: No protocol fee is taken: the factory owner is burned, so feeProtocol can never be turned on.

definitions.fees: Management and performance fees paid by vault investors (the manager's and FBYT's parts), plus the SOL trading fee paid on every vault swap and the SOL fee paid to create a vault.
definitions.revenue: FBYT's share of the management and performance fees, plus all trading and vault creation fees.

definitions.fees: User-paid swap and BNB/WBNB wrapping fees actually credited to WormSwap's fee distributor before protocol allocations, excluding external token transfer taxes, underlying DEX fees, Arena payments and donations.
definitions.revenue: Net swap and wrapping fee receipts retained by WormSwap and allocated entirely to TANUKI buybacks and burns, with no supplier or referral share.
definitions.holders: Net swap and wrapping fee receipts earmarked for TANUKI buybacks and burns, recognized when received rather than again when the burn batch executes.

definitions.fees: The 10% tax traders pay on PSTR buys and sells, plus the USDC yield earned by the PAPER the treasury has staked on Papertrade, valued at the HYPE it is swapped to and counted when the buyback contract spends it. Tax paid by the buyback contract's own purchases is excluded, since it is paid out of that yield.
definitions.revenue: All fees: the trade tax goes to the team and the treasury and the yield goes to the team and the buyback.
definitions.holders: The staking yield the buyback contract spends buying PSTR and burning it, net of the 10% tax it pays on those purchases.

definitions.fees: Taker fees paid by traders whose orders fill against a resting order, at 7% x price x (1 - price) per share, minus fees refunded on trades that failed to settle on Solana; deposit and withdrawal fees are not included.
definitions.revenue: Taker fees kept by Seeryx after paying 20% back to makers as rebates and refunding fees on trades that failed to settle.

definitions.fees: Fees paid by bskts users: the mint fee on buying a basket and the zap-out fee on selling one for USDG, plus each basket's yearly management fee.
definitions.revenue: All mint, zap-out and management fees, kept by the bskts treasury.

definitions.fees: The 2% fee on every buy and sell of a coin launched on Sapling, the flat fee paid to plant a coin, and Sapling's fee on buys, plantings and sales made from a Zcash account. On Robinhood Chain: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee on every buy and sell of a coin planted through Sapling, both paid to Sapling's splitter, plus the planting fee and the Zcash account fee, paid in USDG to the treasury.
definitions.revenue: The part of the 2% coin trading fee Sapling keeps (10% treasury, 25% $SAPLING buyback and burn, 25% $SAPLING/ZEC liquidity), plus the planting fee and the Zcash account fee. On Robinhood Chain the shares apply to what reaches Sapling's splitter: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee.
definitions.holders: 50% of the 2% coin trading fee: 25% buys and burns $SAPLING, and 25% goes to the $SAPLING/ZEC pool on PumpSwap, where about half of it buys $SAPLING, both sides are deposited and the LP tokens are burned, so no one, Sapling included, can withdraw it. On Robinhood Chain the shares apply to what reaches Sapling's splitter: the 2% creator tax plus the creator's 70% of Pons's 1% fee.

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by traders, plus bribes paid to the protocol to attract AERO Rewards to pools.
definitions.revenue: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.
definitions.holders: Swap fees earned by AERO-earning liquidity and bribes, all distributed to sAERO holders.

definitions.fees: Swap fees paid by users

Fees users pay Veil to shield tokens into its private pool, withdraw them, swap privately or fill a private DCA order, plus Veil's share of the relayer fee; network fees, Jupiter's swap fees and tokens swept from closed DCA escrows are not included.
definitions.revenue: All fees users pay Veil for shielding, withdrawals, private swaps and private DCA fills, plus its share of the relayer fee, all kept by Veil as it has no liquidity providers or stakers to pay.
definitions.holders: $VEIL bought on the market with 20% of Veil's revenue and burned, counted from the buyback wallet's on-chain burns at the token's price.

definitions.fees: Arbitrage profit made through the vaults' pools, as each vault's profit splitter pays it out.
definitions.revenue: 25% of the profit: half to the fee jar, which buys GOO and burns it, and half to the development fund.
definitions.holders: 12.5% of the profit, sent to the fee jar, which auctions it for GOO and burns the GOO.

definitions.fees: Actual builder-code fees paid on Hyperliquid perpetual trades carrying ARX's builder code; excludes Hyperliquid exchange trading fees and legacy ARX builder addresses.
definitions.revenue: Builder-code fees received by ARX on Hyperliquid perpetual trades, before any subsequent referral payouts from ARX's treasury.

definitions.fees: EVM chains: swap fees of the pools sasa creates for every coin, counted when sasa's builder collects them: the quote-asset side (ETH, BNB or USDC) and the coin side (in the launched coin, valued where the coin has a price). Solana: the creator fees of coins launched on sasa (both halves).
definitions.revenue: EVM: 70% of the collected swap fees, sent to sasa's fee vault. Solana: sasa's 50% of the creator fees, received by its treasury.

definitions.fees: A 0.25% fee on every cash-out from the Gloam shielded pool. Deposits and private payments are free.
definitions.revenue: All cash-out fees go to the Gloam fee recipient.

definitions.fees: The fee the Stockereum hook charges on every swap, in the quote currency, from the hook's Trade event: 1% on v2 launches, 1%, 2% or 3% (chosen by the creator) on v3 launches, plus the anti-snipe rate in the first moments after a launch.
definitions.revenue: The platform's share of the swap fee: half of the normal 1% on v2, 0.5% of the trade on 1% v3 launches and 1% of the trade on 2% and 3% v3 launches, plus any anti-snipe excess.

definitions.fees: Traders pay the fee tier configured for the pool: 0.01%, 0.05%, 0.30%, or 1%.
definitions.revenue: Protocol revenue is the exact amount emitted as protocolFeesToken0 or protocolFeesToken1 by each swap.

definitions.fees: Router fee (feeAmount in SherwoodSwap events), charged on the input token.
definitions.revenue: All router fees go to the TradeWood treasury.

definitions.fees: All fees traders pay, before any share goes back to Conviction Pool depositors or referrers: opening and closing fees, liquidation closing fees included, plus the borrowing fees paid while a position is open. Funding is paid between traders and is not counted.
definitions.revenue: The share of opening and closing fees Nova keeps (governance fee).

definitions.fees: Total interest paid by borrowers
definitions.revenue: Protocol and holders share of interest
definitions.holders: Share of interest into protocol governance token holders.

definitions.fees: On profitable closes, an impact haircut on the gain and a 2% fee on the gain after the haircut; on losing closes and liquidations, a 2% fee on the margin lost, taken by the protocol from what the LP pool receives.
definitions.revenue: All fees (Win Haircut, Win Fee, Loss Fee) are kept: the haircut stays in the protocol-owned LP pool and the win fee goes to the protocol.

definitions.fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on trades copied through FiatBear; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees collected by FiatBear on copied trades.

definitions.fees: The trading tax (1%-5%, set per launch) paid on every curve and graduated-pool trade, in the quote asset. The pools' 0.05% Uniswap v4 LP fee is not included: it is earned by the pool's liquidity and already counted by the Uniswap v4 adapter.
definitions.revenue: The platform's share of the tax (0.50% of the trade at deployment, frozen into each launch), plus the creator share of launches whose creator wallet is the treasury ($CURB).

definitions.fees: Hyperliquid builder code fees paid by users on perpetual trades placed through Perpex; excludes Hyperliquid's own trading fees.
definitions.revenue: Builder code fees collected by Perpex.

definitions.fees: Every swap in a Phlece coin's Uniswap v4 pool pays a 0.98% base fee plus the creator's 1-10% tax, in the coin's paired asset (QuoteFeeTaken events of each coin's hook). Swaps in a coin's first 3 seconds also pay an anti-snipe surcharge. The pool's own LP fee is 0.
definitions.revenue: 20% of every trading fee (the portal's platformBps) plus the whole anti-snipe surcharge go to the Phlece team Safe.

definitions.fees: The fees players pay on settled positions: the open fee on each deposit and the 10% profit fee on a gain.
definitions.revenue: The fees less the creator royalty: the protocol's share and the $OVER holders' share.
definitions.holders: 25% of the profit fees: from $OVER positions to the $OVER stakers' rewards, from USDG positions to $OVER buybacks.

definitions.fees: Builder Fees collected from Orderly Network
definitions.revenue: All the fees collected

definitions.fees: Platform fees paid in USDG on every token and stock token trade made in Onagi (transfers into the Onagi fee vault), plus all Pons V2 swap fees and creator tax charged on ONAGI token trades (curve and graduated pool sweep events). Platform fees include a small reimbursement for network gas that Onagi pays on behalf of users, which is not separated on chain.
definitions.revenue: Platform fees plus the creator share of ONAGI token swap fees that Pons credits to Onagi.
definitions.holders: 75% of revenue: 50% is paid to eligible ONAGI holders in USDG and 25% buys ONAGI and sends it to the burn address. Computed from Onagi's published split.

definitions.fees: Fees paid by traders of tokens launched on Grainpad (Solana): Grainpad's platform fee (0.75% under its current config) and the token creator's fee (0.25%) on every trade against the Raydium LaunchLab bonding curves it configures, and, once a token graduates, the quote-side trading fees of its permanently locked liquidity, harvested with the Fee Keys Grainpad holds, plus the creator fee of those graduated pools, counted when the launch's creator claims it. Raydium's own protocol fee and the token transfer taxes of Grainpad reward launches are excluded. Amounts are in each pool's quote token, mostly wXMR.
definitions.revenue: The platform fee and the harvested locked-liquidity fees, both received by Grainpad.

definitions.fees: SKALE uses sFUEL (SKALE Fuel), a gas token distributed FREE via faucets. While transactions consume gas on-chain, sFUEL has $0 monetary value. User fees are $0.

definitions.holders: No sFUEL is burned or distributed as revenue since it has no value. Revenue model is entirely based on SKL token staking.

definitions.revenue: Share of the transaction fee kept by the chain's FeeCollector treasury. This is the whole fee today, because the block proposer share is configured at 0 basis points.
